question: Which Pratihara ruler started the tripartite conflict of Kannauj by defeating the Pala king Dharmapala?
solution: Vatsaraja is considered to be the real powerful king of the Pratihara Empire. He attempted to conquer Kannauj but was defeated by the Rashtrakuta king Dhruva.

question: Which ruler of Pala dynasty shifted his capital to Mudagiri (Munger)?
solution: At the time of Devpal, the Pala dynasty had established its influence from the Himalayas to the Vindhyas and from the Arabian Sea to the Bay of Bengal.

question: By whom was the Prakrit play named 'Karpoormanjari' composed?
solution: Rajashekhar was the courtier of Gurjara-Pratihara kings Mahendrapal and Mahipal. His works give good information about the society and geography of that time.

question: Jagannath Puri Temple (Orissa) was built by the rulers of which dynasty?
solution: Jagannath Temple is called 'White Pagoda'. This temple is world famous for its annual Rath Yatra. Lord Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra are worshiped here.

question: Who held the title 'Maduraiyum Elamam Konda' during the Chola period?
solution: Prantaka I fought a war with the Rashtrakutas in the last years of his rule, in which he suffered defeat and the Chola Empire collapsed for some time.

question: What was the function of 'Ottar' in Chola administration?
options: The elephant drivers of the army were called Gaj-padai.
Royal spies who brought information about the empire in disguise
The tax collecting employees were called revenue officers.
solution: The Cholas had a huge spy network through which they kept an eye on their feudal lords and officials. This was important for internal security.

question: What is the top part of 'Shikhar' of 'Dravidian style' and 'Nagar style' temples called respectively?
solution: A golden Kalash was often placed on top of the Stupika, which was called 'Shikhar-Kalash'. This was the highest point of the sanctity of the temple. In Chola temples the Stupika was made very strongly.

question: What was the function of the committee called 'Iri Variyam' during the Chola period?
solution: The Uttaramerur inscription describes several 'variyam' (committees) such as Totta Variyam (garden committee) and Erivariam (reservoir committee). This shows his efficient rural management.

question: For what was the word 'Valan' used in the Chola period?
solution: Ownership of agricultural land was important during the Chola period. Wealthy farmers (Vellalas) had great influence in local administration.

question: What are the three main styles of 'Kalinga Architecture'?
options: Rekha Deul, Pidha Deul and Khakhara Deul
solution: The Lingaraja and Jagannath temples of Odisha are examples of 'Rekha Deul', while the Jagamohana of Konark is an example of 'Pidha Deul'.

question: Which ruler of the Gurjara-Pratihar dynasty stopped the Arabs from entering India, due to which he is also called the 'destroyer of Mlechchas'?
solution: Nagabhata I was the real founder of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty. Arab writers have greatly praised the power of the Pratiharas and their cavalry.

question: What type of information is mainly given in the book 'Brahman Sarvasva'?
options: There were separate texts on the art of war.
solution: The Sena rulers were patrons of orthodox Hinduism. He promoted such texts to organize the society according to the Vedas and Smritis.

question: Why is Lord Shiva called 'Hari-Hara' in 'Lingaraja Temple' of Odisha?
options: Because the temple is on the banks of Ganga
Because its priests were named Hari and Shiva
Because the color of the temple is green (Hari)
Because there the combined power of both Shiva (Hara) and Vishnu (Hari) is considered.
solution: Elements of both trident and chakra are found in the weapons installed on the peak of Lingaraja temple. This reflects the religious tolerance of medieval India.

question: Which South Indian Chola king defeated the Pala king Mahipala I?
solution: Mahipala I is called the 'second founder' of the Pala dynasty because he re-organized the empire, but he failed to stop the Chola armies.

question: For what purpose was 'Shalbhog' land used during the Chola period?
options: To maintain schools and educational institutions
solution: Schools were often run in the precincts of Chola temples. The income from Shalbhog land ensured the salaries of teachers and food for students.

question: Who was the Chola king when the Chola navy conquered the islands of Maldives?
solution: Rajaraja I had proved his naval superiority by defeating the Chera navy at 'Kandalur Shala'.

question: What is the pillared hall built in front of the sanctum sanctorum in 'Nagar style' temples called?
solution: Khajuraho temples have many pavilions such as ardha-mandapa, mandapa and maha-mandapa. It shows the gradual journey of the devotee towards the sanctum sanctorum.

question: Who established the 'Sena dynasty' after the decline of the Pala dynasty?
solution: The rulers of Sena dynasty called themselves 'Brahma-Kshatriya'. He revived Hinduism by reducing the influence of Buddhism of the Pala dynasty.

question: Which ruler of the Pala dynasty extended his power up to the Arabian Sea, which is mentioned by Arab writers?
solution: During the time of Devpal, the Pala dynasty greatly promoted trade relations with South-East Asia and the Arab world. The Arab traveler Suleiman has called the Pala Empire 'Ruhmi'.

question: What was the function of 'Puravu-vari-tinaikkalam' department in Chola administration?
solution: The Cholas had conducted a very detailed survey of the land (like during the time of Rajaraja I). The units of measurement were very precise, making revenue management efficient.

question: What is the main feature of 'Gangekondacholapuram' temple built by Chola king Rajendra I?
options: It is a symbol of victory over Ganga
It is made only of wood
solution: Rajendra I had taken the title of 'Gangekondachola'. The vimana of this temple is smaller than that of the Brihadeshwara temple at Thanjavur but is much richer in carvings.

question: Chola king Rajendra I, as the 'Napoleon of South India', demonstrated his naval power and defeated the king of which country?
solution: After the conquest of Sri Lanka, Rajendra Chola built many grand temples there and made it an integral part of the Chola Empire.

question: What type of heroine has Rajashekhar described in the play 'Karpoormanjari'?
solution: The specialty of Karpoormanjari is that it is written entirely in 'Shauraseni Prakrit' language, which shows the linguistic command of Rajasekhara.

question: The huge statue of which animal is installed in the 'Lingaraja Temple' of Odisha which is known as the vehicle of Shiva?
solution: Symbols of both Shiva and Vishnu are found in the courtyard of Lingaraja temple, which is indicative of the religious coordination of that time.

question: 'Kudavolai' system was applicable at which level of Chola administration?
solution: Committees elected on the Kudavolai system managed ponds, roads, temples and justice. This is a great example of democracy in ancient India.

question: Who wrote the book 'Bhuvankosh', which describes the geography of the then known world?
solution: From the works of Rajashekhar, we get information about the boundaries of the states and the condition of the rivers of that time.

question: Which mountains of North India have been described by Rajashekhar in 'Kavyamimansa'?
solution: Rajasekhar's works are not only literary, but they are also considered extremely reliable as historical and geographical sources.

question: How many years was the tenure of the members of 'Variam' committees in the Chola administration?
solution: If any member was found corrupt after the elections, he was immediately removed and his relatives were also banned from contesting the elections.

question: Which Chola ruler had built the huge lake named 'Cholagangam'?
solution: The Chola rulers were experts in irrigation engineering. Cholagangam Lake was 16 miles long and was built to commemorate the conquest of Bengal.

question: What is the sanctum part of the temple called in 'Orissa Architecture'?
solution: Temples in Odisha consist of four main parts: Deul (sanctum sanctorum), Jagamohana (mandapam), Nat Mandapam (dance hall) and Bhoga Mandapa (dining hall).

question: Chola king Rajendra I waged a naval war against which empire to establish his authority as 'Napoleon of the East'?
solution: Rajendra Chola had such a powerful navy that he called the Bay of Bengal 'Chola Lake'. It symbolizes the golden age of the Indian Navy.

question: Which Chola king is called the 'Napoleon of the South' and he took the title of 'Gangekondachola' after conquering the Ganges?
solution: Rajendra I conquered the whole of Sri Lanka and launched a successful naval invasion of the Srivijaya Empire in South-East Asia. During his time the Chola navy was the most powerful in the world.

question: What was the meaning of 'Perumandam' in Chola administration?
solution: The king was not bound to take the advice of the Perumandam, but this council was of great importance in determining the policies of governance.

question: In the 'Uttarmerur' election during the Chola period, if a member had been a member of any committee for the last five years, could he contest the election again?
options: Yes, if he is the king's favorite
Yes, if he did a very good job
solution: The Cholas laid great emphasis on decentralization and rotation of power. This was a wonderful way of maintaining freshness in governance.

question: How many chariot wheels are there in the Konark temple, famous as 'Black Pagoda'?
solution: Konark Temple is designed in the form of a huge chariot of Lord Surya. This temple is known for its intricate carvings and astronomical accuracy.

question: Which Pratihara king was defeated by the Pala ruler Dharmapala?
solution: The sequence of victory and defeat in the tripartite conflict kept changing. Dharampala took the title of 'Uttarapath Swami' after gaining control over Kannauj.

question: Which is the famous inscription giving information about Gurjara-Pratihara ruler Mihir Bhoj?
solution: Mihir Bhoj was the greatest ruler of the Pratihara dynasty. In the Gwalior inscription he has been called 'Adivaraha'. During his time the Pratiharas had established their permanent control over Kannauj.

question: Who was the real founder of the Chola Empire who conquered 'Madurai' and took the title of 'Maduraikonda'?
solution: Prantaka I was defeated by the Rashtrakuta king Krishna III in the battle of Takkolam. The Uttarmerur inscription, which gives information about village administration, dates back to the period of Prantaka I.

question: In which posture is Lord Shiva seen in the famous 'Nataraja' sculpture of the Chola period?
solution: The idol of Nataraja was made of bronze. Below the right foot of Shiva is a demon called 'Apasmara' which represents ignorance. His four hands symbolize different powers.

question: Why did Chola king Rajendra I receive the title of 'Napoleon of South India' (by historians)?
options: Because he made modern war policies
Because he was a friend of France
Due to their invincible military campaigns and maritime expansion, they spread the Chola flag to North India, Sri Lanka and South-East Asia.
Because they created a new constitution
solution: Rajendra I had the largest navy of that time. He established his power not only on land but also on the sea, which makes him a great military genius.

question: What was the main difference between 'Ur' and 'Sabha' in the Chola period?
options: Ur was an organization of traders
Ur was the assembly of the general public and Sabha of Brahmins
Ur was only for the army
The meeting was only for women
solution: The functioning of the assembly was very democratic. All work was done through committees and their members were selected on the basis of strict eligibility criteria.

question: What is the specialty of 'Vesara Style' temples?
options: It is found only in North India
There is no sanctum sanctorum in it
It is a mixture of Nagara and Dravidian styles
Only wood is used in this
solution: The Chalukya and Hoysala kings of Badami promoted the Vesara style. This style symbolizes the cultural union of North and South India.

question: Who was called 'Ajnapati' in Chola administration?
options: The head of the village was called Muvendavelan or Araiyar.
The officer who executed the orders of the king.
solution: There was a complex process of recording the oral orders of the Chola king in written form and transmitting them to the local level.

question: What type of tax was 'Vetti' during the Chola period?
solution: The list of taxes during the Chola period was very long. Kadmai was the main land tax which constituted about one-third of the crop. Vetti was used in public works.

question: What were the local taxes collected by the assembly of 'Nadu' during the Chola period called?
solution: The distribution of taxes was clear in the Chola administration. Village taxes went to the village, Nadu taxes went to the Nadu and the main taxes went to the king's treasury.

question: In which language did Rajashekhar compose the texts 'Bal Ramayana' and 'Bal Mahabharata'?
solution: Rajashekhar presented the stories of Ramayana and Mahabharata in a condensed and dramatic form. He was a symbol of the literary pride of the Pratiharas.

question: Which ruler of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty assumed the title of 'Adivaraha' and issued coins symbolizing the Varaha incarnation of Lord Vishnu?
solution: Mihir Bhoj was described by the Arab traveler Suleiman as 'the enemy of Islam' and one of the four greatest kings of the world. Bhoj's victories are described in the Gwalior Prashasti.

question: What was the main function of the 'Nandeshi' trading association during the Chola period?
solution: The Indian traders were very powerful. They also had private armies for their security. They were given special privileges by the kings.

question: Who was the founder of the Pala dynasty who was chosen by the local leaders to end anarchy?
solution: The rulers of Pala dynasty were followers of Buddhism. Gopal established peace in Bengal and laid the foundation of a stable rule. After him Dharampal played an active role in the struggle for Kannauj.

question: Chola king Rajaraja I built a grand temple of Lord Shiva in Thanjavur, with which stone was it built?
solution: The shikhara (vimana) of the Brihadeshwara temple is made of a single granite stone (about 80 tonnes), called 'Kumbham'. Reaching it to such a height still remains a mystery.

question: According to the Uttarmerur inscription, by what method were the members of village committees elected during the Chola period?
solution: To become a member of the village committee, a person should have his own land, house and he should have knowledge of the Vedas. Thieves or criminals could not contest elections.

question: What are the pyramidal layers in the roof of the pavilions of 'Kalinga style' temples called?
solution: When seen from outside the roof of Pidha looks like stairs on top of stairs. This design was very strong and was capable of withstanding heavy rainfall.

question: Who was called 'Manram' during the Chola period?
options: The village justice place or platform
solution: The Chola judicial system was very simple and accessible. Small disputes were settled at the local level, while serious crimes were judged by the king or high officials.

question: In which of his books has 'Rajshekhar' called Pratihar king Mahendrapal as 'Raghukul Tilak'?
solution: The Pratiharas considered themselves descendants of Lakshman (brother of Lord Rama), hence the terms 'Raghuvansh' or 'Raghukul' were used for them.

question: In which of his books has 'Rajashekhar' described the various rivers of India and the states situated on their banks?
solution: Rajashekhar's geographical information was so accurate that he can also be called the 'geographer of Pratiharas'. He has mentioned areas from Kashmir to Kanyakumari.

question: What was 'Kalanju' in the Chola period?
options: Gold coin and unit of weight
solution: The Chola economy was very developed. Kalanju was used in international trade, especially trade with South-East Asia.

question: What is the roof of the pavilion (jagamohana) of 'Kalinga style' temples?
options: It did not have a roof
solution: The Pidha Deul was used so that the height and grandeur of the main sanctum (Deul) was more clearly visible.

question: What is the specialty of 'Vaital Deul' (Bhubaneswar) temple of Odisha?
options: It is dedicated to the Sun
solution: The architecture of Vaital Deul resembles the South Indian Dravidian style 'Gopuram', reflecting the cultural exchange of that time.

question: During the Pala period, 'Atisha Dipankar' went to Tibet and spread the teachings of which major Buddhist monastery?
solution: In Tibet, Atisha is respected like the 'second Buddha'. He purified the Buddhism there and laid the foundation of 'Kadampa' sect.

question: Which Rashtrakuta king defeated the Pala ruler Dharmapala, after which Dharmapala refused to accept him as 'Uttarapatha Swami'?
solution: The power of the Rashtrakuta kings was so great that they came from south to north and defeated both the Palas and Pratiharas, but they did not stay in North India for long.

question: Which famous Muslim invaders attacked Bengal during the time of Lakshman Sen, the last ruler of the Sen dynasty?
solution: Lakshman Sen had fled through the back door without fighting, which led to the end of Sen power in Bengal and the beginning of Ottoman rule.

question: Which king assumed the title 'Maduraikonda' during the Chola period?
solution: Prantaka I was an early king of the expansionist period of the Cholas. He also invaded Sri Lanka, but his expansion was halted for some time due to defeat by the Rashtrakutas.

question: Which ruler of Pala dynasty donated the revenue of 100 villages for the maintenance of Vikramshila University?
solution: Vikramshila University became the rival of Nalanda at that time. From here many scholars went to Tibet and Central Asia.

question: The 'Nataraja' idol of Lord Shiva made by the Cholas is made of which metal and by what technique is it made?
solution: In the idol of Nataraja, Shiva is shown performing the Tandava dance. He is standing over a demon named 'Apasmar' (symbol of ignorance). This sculpture shows the artistic skill of the Cholas.

question: Which great scholar and historical treatise was composed during the time of 'Rampala' in the last phase of decline of Pala dynasty which compares Rampal with Lord Rama?
solution: From Sandhyakar Nandi's Ramcharita, we get important historical information about the last years of the Pala period and the Kaivarta rebellion.

question: Apart from Jaydev, who else was included in the 'Pancharatna' of the court of Sen king Lakshman Sen?
solution: Laxman Sen's court was a big center of literature. Halayudha had composed a book named 'Brahmana Sarvasva'. Sanskrit literature developed a lot during this period.

question: Which Sen ruler composed the texts named 'Danasagar' and 'Adbhutsagar'?
solution: The Sen rulers were great patrons of literature and education. Ballal Sen played a big role in social reforms and revival of Hinduism in Bengal.

question: Sanskrit poet and playwright Rajashekhar, who is called 'Kalidas of Pratiharas', graced whose court?
solution: Rajashekhar's major works include Bal Ramayana, Bal Mahabharata, Vidhasalbhanjika and Bhuvankosh. At the time of Mahendrapala, the Pratihara Empire extended from Punjab to Bengal.

question: Which part of Sri Lanka was conquered by the Chola king Rajaraja I and made 'Mummadicholamandalam' a province of the Chola Empire?
solution: Rajaraja I destroyed Anuradhapura and made Polonnaruwa his new capital. He also built a Shiva temple there.

question: What shape is the entrance gate (Toran) of 'Mukteshwar Temple' of Odisha?
options: There is no toran in it
solution: The Mukteshwar Temple is also called the 'Child Temple' of Kalinga architecture as it combines all the elementary elements of the style with perfection.

question: Which ruler of the Pala dynasty maintained close relations with the Shailendra dynasty rulers of Java (Indonesia)?
solution: The Pala rulers were not only the kings of Bengal, but they were also internationally renowned as patrons of Buddhism. Trade and cultural ties with South-East Asia were very strong during his time.

question: Which Rashtrakuta king defeated both the Pala king Dharmapala and the Pratihara king Vatsaraja during the tripartite conflict?
solution: Dhruva had defeated the Rashtrakutas in the battle of Kannauj. Although the Rashtrakutas never created a permanent kingdom in North India, they came only for conquest and plunder.

question: In which style was 'Lingaraja Temple' (Bhubaneswar) of Odisha constructed?
solution: Lingaraja Temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva (Hari-Hara). Its construction was started by Somvanshi king Yayati Keshari. The main peak of the temple is very high and impressive.

question: Who was the author of the book 'Kavyamimansa', which is based on literary criticism?
solution: From the works of Rajashekhar we get information about the cultural condition of India in the 10th century. He has described the customs and traditions of both North and South India.

question: 'Peruman' was the honorific term used for whom in the Chola administration?
options: For the commander, he was called Mahadandanayak.
For the chief priest, he was called a religious preacher.
For big traders, they were called Nanadesi or Veer Vanik.
solution: Chola kings built grand temples to show their power and prestige. He considered himself an incarnation or part of Shiva.

question: What were called 'Perundaram' and 'Sirutaram' during the Chola dynasty?
options: The two types of military units
solution: The Chola kings had a large and efficient bureaucracy. Officials were often paid in the form of land.

question: Why was it mandatory for a candidate to have his own house to contest elections for 'Variam' committees in the Chola administration?
options: So that he could work from home
To ensure his social prestige and responsibility, it was believed that only the person who can manage his own house can handle the administration of the village.
Because the king did not like homeless people
So that he does not live on rent
solution: There was great emphasis on transparency and morality in the Chola electoral system. If a candidate did not give his property details, he was disqualified.

question: What is the small space between the sanctum sanctorum and the pavilion in 'Dravidian style' temples called?
solution: The interval is found in both Nagara and Dravidian styles. It serves as a transition zone between the external noise and internal peace of the temple.

question: How many horses are shown pulling the chariot in the carvings of Konark temple?
solution: The Sun Temple of Konark is the pinnacle of medieval Indian architecture. Its horses are a symbol of speed and power.

question: Which part of Lingaraja Temple (Orissa) is called 'Jagamohana'?
options: The entrance gate can be called Singhdwar.
The flag pillar is called Arun Stambh (like in Konark).
solution: Jagmohan is usually built in 'Pidha Deul' style with a terraced roof. Apart from Vimana and Jagamohan, Lingaraja temple also has Nat Mandir and Bhog Mandap.

question: What was the village 'Uttaramrur' famous for during the Chola period?
options: Kanchipuram was famous for its silk sarees.
Known for its strong naval cantonment
For its advanced village administration system and inscriptions
solution: The Uttaramarur inscriptions reveal that the village was divided into 30 wards (Kudumbas) and a committee member was elected from each ward.

question: The structures built on the roof of 'Pidha Deul' in the temples of Odisha are called 'Pidha', what is their number usually?
options: The thickness of all the layers was equal
There were no layers in them
solution: This terraced roof of Pidha Deul created a cool and airy environment inside the pavilion for the devotees.

question: According to the 'Uttarmerur' inscription in the Chola administration, what was the punishment if a person failed to account for his property?
options: He and his relatives were permanently banned from contesting elections
He was thrown out of the village
solution: Moral purity was the highest priority in the Chola electoral system. This is also a big lesson for the modern era that anyone holding public office should be transparent.

question: What was attached to the uppermost part of the 'Rekha Deul' (above the Kalash) in 'Kalinga style' temples?
solution: The curved peak of Rekha Deul was a symbol of the power and divinity that connects to the universe above.

question: Which dynasty ruled Bengal after the fall of the Pala dynasty and revived orthodox Hinduism (Brahminism)?
solution: The real founder of the Sena dynasty was Vijayasena. Ballal Sen had started 'elitism'. The last important ruler of this dynasty was Lakshman Sen in whose court Jaydev lived.

question: What type of lighting was arranged in the sanctum sanctorum of 'Rekha Deul' in the temples of Odisha?
options: It was completely dark and quiet
solution: The darkness of Deul and dim light of Jagmohan symbolized the taking of the devotee from the material world to the spiritual world.

question: Apart from 'Jagmohan' and 'Deul', which is the other major part in Konark Sun Temple where dance and musical programs were held?
solution: The carvings of the Nat temple depict the postures of the famous Odissi dance of Odisha. This is proof of the artistic vibrancy of that time.

question: What is the shape of 'Khakhara Deula' in 'Kalinga style' temples?
solution: Khakhara Deul was mainly used for tantric worship and goddess temples (e.g. Bhuvaneshwari, Chamunda). Vaital Deul of Bhubaneswar is the best example of this.

question: Jayadeva, the author of the famous Sanskrit text 'Gita Govinda', was the court poet of which dynasty?
solution: 'Dhakeshwari Temple' in Dhaka was built by Ballal Sen during the time of Sen dynasty. In 1204, Bakhtiyar Khilji attacked Lakshman Sen and ended this dynasty.

question: What was the tax-free land donated to Brahmins during the Chola period called?
solution: The Chola rulers donated land to various communities. The land given to Jain institutions was called 'Pallichchandam'. Land revenue was the main source of income of the empire.

question: What kind of stone carvings are there in 'Lingaraja Temple' which makes it the 'pinnacle of Odisha Architecture'?
solution: The spire of Lingaraja temple is 180 feet high. Various gods, goddesses, nymphs and scenes of daily life have been carved with great detail on its walls.

question: Which king assumed the title of 'Bangaladeshwar' during the Sena dynasty?
solution: Vijayasena is considered to be the real powerful king of the Sena dynasty. He ruled for more than 60 years and created a stable administrative structure.

question: Which Pala ruler founded 'Sompura Mahavihara' (present-day Bangladesh)?
solution: Buddhist art and education developed greatly during the reign of the Pala dynasty rulers. Sompura Mahavihara was the largest educational institution in South Asia at that time.

question: What were 'Manigramam' and 'Anjuvannam' in the Chola period?
solution: Trade was very organized during the time of Cholas. Manigramam category is also mentioned in the inscriptions of South-East Asia, which shows their trading expansion.

question: What are the floors above the sanctum sanctorum in 'Dravidian style' temples called?
solution: The vimana of Brihadeshwar temple is 13 storeys. An 80 ton stone has been placed on its top floor, which is a marvel of ancient construction art.

question: The tripartite conflict ended with the final victory of which dynasty and their capture of Kannauj?
solution: The tripartite conflict lasted for almost 200 years. This weakened the central authority of India which later gave way to the Turkish invaders.

question: According to the 'Uttamerur' inscription in the Chola period, what should have been the age of the person contesting the election?
solution: Apart from age, the person should have knowledge of the Vedas and the ability to write a commentary on at least one Veda. This shows how much importance education had in the Chola administration.

question: Who was the author of the book 'Harivilas', which is based on Lord Krishna?
solution: Rajasekhar's versatile talent makes him stand apart among the scholars of his time. He had mastered Sanskrit as well as Prakrit.

question: Which stone has been mainly used in the construction of Konark Sun Temple?
solution: Iron beams were also used in the Konark temple which is a testimony to the engineering skills of that time.

question: Which Pratihara king has been portrayed by Rajashekhar as the husband of 'Kapoormanjari' in the play 'Viddhashalabhanjika'?
solution: Rajashekhar's works give a vivid depiction of the grandeur of the court, the splendor of makeup and the luxury of the then society.

question: What was the original name of Chola king Rajaraja I?
solution: Rajaraja I was a great conqueror and efficient administrator. He made the Chola power the undisputed leader of South India.

question: Which famous painting style developed during the time of Pala kings which was mainly done on palm leaves?
solution: Bright colors were used in Pala painting. Texts like 'Prajnaparamita' were decorated with these pictures. This style later reached Nepal and Tibet.

question: What was the most unique feature of the Chola administration for which they are famous in history?
solution: The Chola empire was divided into Mandalam, Valanadu and Nadu. Institutions like 'Ur' (assembly of common people) and 'Sabha' (assembly of Brahmins) functioned at the village level.

question: Who was called 'Nagaram' during the Chola period?
options: The settlements inside the forts were called Padavidu.
The assembly of merchants and trading centers
solution: Nagaram was an important part of the Chola economy. They also gave loans to the king and provided financial assistance in the construction of temples.

question: When Mahmud Ghaznavi attacked Kannauj in 1018 AD, who was the ruler of the Pratihar dynasty who surrendered without fighting?
solution: The main reason for the decline of the Pratiharas was foreign invasion and the independence of their feudal lords. The attack of Mahmud Ghaznavi broke the back of the Pratihara power.

question: Chola king Rajendra I assumed the title of 'Gangekondachola', what is its literal meaning?
options: Cholas living on the banks of Ganga
solution: The main objective of Rajendra I's Bengal campaign was to demonstrate his power. He had poured the Ganga water brought from there into a pond named 'Cholagangam'.

question: What were the verandahs built around the main temple in 'Dravidian style' temples called?
solution: In Chola temples these verandahs were often very high and pillared. These pillars had beautiful carvings of Chola history and mythology.

question: At which place did the Chola king Rajaraja I allow the Buddhist king Sailendra (Java) to build a Buddha Vihara?
solution: This incident is a testimony to the religious tolerance of the Chola kings and their friendly relations with the Shailendra kings of Java. The Chola kings themselves were devotees of Shiva but respected other religions.

question: Of the 24 wheels of the Konark Sun Temple, how many spokes are there in each wheel representing the time?
solution: Each wheel of Konark temple works like a sun dial. Even today the time can be determined accurately by its shadow.

question: What was the main function of the huge stone (Kumbham) placed on the top of 'Dravidian style' temples?
options: Providing balance and stability to the structure of the temple, it acted as a keystone that centered the weight of the entire vimana.
It was not possible to climb to such a height to keep an eye on the enemy from there.
To keep the gold urn there
solution: The 80 ton Kumbham of the Thanjavur temple proves that the Cholas had advanced mechanical and engineering knowledge at that time.

question: Which Pala ruler founded the famous Vikramshila University?
solution: Dharampal had assumed the title of 'Paramasaugata'. He defeated Indrayudh, the ruler of Kannauj, and appointed Chakrayudh as his puppet ruler there and took the title of 'Uttarapatha Swami'.

question: The famous scholar Halayudha, who composed 'Brahmanasarvasva', was the chief judge (Dharmadhikari) of?
solution: Halayudha attempted to codify Hindu laws and customs. His texts are still important for the social history of medieval Bengal.

question: Who was called 'Kurram' in Chola administration?
options: The dancers of the temples were called 'Devdasi'.
solution: The Chola administration had a hierarchical division: Mandalam > Valanadu > Nadu > Kurram > Ur. This system helped in running the government smoothly.

question: Thanjavur, the capital of the Cholas, was situated on the banks of which river?
solution: The efficient management of the Kaveri river water was the main reason for the agricultural prosperity of the Cholas. He built many dams and canals on the Kaveri.

question: The famous 'Brihadeshwara Temple' (Rajarajeshwara Temple) of Thanjavur was built by which Chola ruler?
solution: Rajaraja I conquered the northern part of Sri Lanka and also captured the Maldives. He also got the land surveyed for the land revenue system.

question: Which empire of South-East Asia was successfully attacked by the Chola navy during the reign of Rajendra I?
solution: The main objective of Rajendra I's naval campaign was to secure the sea trade route and obtain a monopoly on trade with China. This is the only major foreign naval expedition in Indian history.

question: In which part of India is the 'Dravidian style' of temple architecture mainly found?
solution: In Dravidian style temples, the entrance is called 'Gopuram' and the tower above the main temple is called 'Vimana'. Its specialty is having a large reservoir or tank inside the temple.

question: What is the striped circular structure just below the Kalash located on the top of 'Rekha Deul' style temples called?
solution: The sacred Kalash is placed on top of Amlak. The structure of Lingaraj temple is very big and impressive.

question: What was approximately the weight of the gold currency called 'Kalanju' during the Chola period?
solution: The value of Kalanju was decided on the basis of the purity of its gold. It is used extensively in Chola inscriptions in descriptions of loans, donations and taxes.

question: What was the weight and metal of the currency called 'Kasu' in the Chola administration?
solution: The coins of the Cholas were made to facilitate trade. 'Gangekondachola' was inscribed on the coins of Rajendra Chola.

question: What is the path made around the sanctum sanctorum in 'Nagar style' temples called?
solution: In Nagara style the circumambulation path is often covered (Sandhara). It is considered a spiritual way of moving around the sacred energy of the temple.

question: Which Sena ruler was praised by Kalhan, the author of 'Rajatarangini'?
solution: Kalhana's Rajatarangini is an important historical text of the 12th century. It throws light on the relations between various kings of contemporary India.

question: What was the local council that looked after 'Nadu' called in the Chola administration?
solution: The level of decentralization in the Chola administration was so deep that there was autonomy even at the Nadu level. The Cholas used 'Nadu' as an administrative and geographical unit.

question: By what name were gold coins known during the Chola period?
solution: The coins of the Cholas show their power and prosperity in trade. Their coins had symbols of tiger (symbol of Cholas) and fish (symbol of victory over Pandyas).

question: Statues of which two sacred rivers are found at the entrance of the sanctum sanctorum of 'Kalinga style' temples?
solution: The idols of Ganga and Yamuna convey to the devotees that they have symbolically taken a bath in these sacred rivers before entering the temple.

question: Which famous Buddhist monk visited Tibet during the reign of Pala dynasty and played an important role in propagating Buddhism there?
solution: The Pala rulers were great patrons of Buddhism. He endowed the universities of Nalanda and Vikramashila, which spread Buddhism throughout Asia.

question: What was the main function of 'Manram' in Chola administration?
solution: In the Chola administration, justice was accessible only at the local level. The village people themselves resolved their disputes, which reduced the burden on the government.

question: Who composed the Sanskrit play named 'Viddashalbhanjika'?
solution: Beautiful descriptions of women and court etiquette are glimpsed in Rajashekhar's works. He was a very favorite scholar of the Pratihar kings.

question: Who were the 'Velaikkaras' in the Chola administration?
options: The king's personal bodyguards who were ready to sacrifice their lives
solution: The Velaikkar soldiers were famous for their loyalty to the king. They often sacrificed themselves on the death of the king.

question: Who was called 'Kudumbus' in Chola administration?
options: The king's bodyguards were called Velaikkar.
solution: The Kudumbas system ensured that every part of the village was represented in the Gram Sabha. This is an ancient form of the modern 'ward' system.

question: Chola king Rajaraja I took the title of 'Mummadichola', what is its meaning?
options: The one who has three eyes
The Chola who wore three crowns (Chola, Chera, Pandya)
The Chola who lost the battle thrice
The Chola who has three queens
solution: Chola kings took grand titles on the basis of their conquests. Mummadichol was one of the most popular titles of Rajaraja.

question: Who was given the title 'Muvendavelan' in the Chola administration?
options: The soldier who has won three wars
The merchant who traded with three countries was given different respects.
The Brahmin who received donation of three villages was called Trivedi or Chaturvedi.
The prosperous farmer who served the three kings
solution: Chola kings developed such titles to include local influential people in their administration. This reduced the possibility of local rebellion.

question: What is the main difference between the 'Vimana' of Chola period temples and the 'Shikhara' of Nagara style?
options: The vimana is made only of wood
The vimana is pyramidal while the shikhara is curved
Shikhar is found only in South India
solution: The Vimana of the Brihadeshwara temple at Thanjavur is 216 feet high and is considered the highest achievement of Dravidian architecture. On the contrary, the peak of Nagar style is found in the temples of Khajuraho.

question: Why did Chola king Rajaraja I assume the title of 'Shivapadshekhar'?
options: Because they stole the idol of Shiva
Because he was a great war commander
Because of his deep devotion towards Shiva
solution: Rajaraja I was a staunch Shaivite, but he also showed tolerance towards Buddhism and allowed the Buddha Vihara to be built at Nagapattinam.

question: Which three dynasties were involved in the tripartite struggle for control of Kannauj between the 8th and 10th centuries?
solution: The Kannauj Trilateral War was fought to establish political dominance over North India. The Pala dynasty was active in the Bengal region, the Gurjara-Pratiharas in Rajasthan and Gujarat, while the Rashtrakutas invaded northwards from the Maharashtra and Karnataka region.

question: The sculptures of 'Bhukuti' and 'Maitreya' in the art of Pala period belong to which religion?
solution: Pala art developed a distinctive style of bronze sculptures which was carried forward by artists named 'Dhiman' and 'Vitpal'.

question: Which deity is worshiped in 'Lingaraja Temple' of Odisha?
solution: The confluence (Hari-Hara) of both Shiva and Vishnu is considered to be in the Lingaraja temple. There are more than 100 small temples in the temple complex.

question: What is the round stone located above the main peak in the 'Nagar style' temples of North India called?
solution: The main feature of Nagara style temples is their curved shikhara. The most magnificent form of Nagara style can be seen in the Kandariya Mahadev Temple of Khajuraho.

question: What is the name of the pillar located in the courtyard of Konark Sun Temple which was later taken to Puri?
solution: Arun Pillar is dedicated to 'Arun', the charioteer of the Sun. It was shifted from Konark to Puri during the Maratha period.

question: Which Gurjara-Pratihara king made Kannauj his permanent capital?
solution: Nagabhata II also defeated the Arabs and took the title of 'Parambhattarak Maharajadhiraja'. He ended his life by taking water samadhi in the Ganges.

question: By what name is 'Mukteshwar Temple' of Odisha known?
solution: Mukteshwar Temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva. Its toran gate (entrance) shows a beautiful blend of Buddhist and Hindu styles.

question: What was the committee that administered justice within 'Nadu' called during the Chola period?
solution: Fine (Danda) was the most common punishment in the Chola judicial system. The fine was often taken in the form of donations to temples or lighting of lamps there.

question: What did 'Valanadu' mean in the Chola administration?
options: The Chola Empire was divided into Mandalams (provinces), which were further divided into Valanadus and then into Nadus (districts).
solution: The Chola administration was very organized. The group of villages was called 'Kurram'. The role of Ur (assembly of common people) and Sabha (assembly of Brahmins) was important in local self-governance.

question: Where was the main center of 'Manigramam' business organization during the Chola period?
solution: Manigramam traders were exempted from toll taxes by the Chola kings and owned fleets of sea vessels.

question: Which Pala ruler donated the revenue of five villages for a monastery at Nalanda at the request of the Sailendra dynasty king Balaputradeva of Java?
solution: Devapala strengthened the Pala navy and turned his attention to foreign missions. The famous Buddhist monks Dipankara Atisha and Dharmaswami were active during his reign.

question: Who completed the book 'Adbhuta Sagar' during the Sena dynasty?
solution: The contribution of Sen rulers to literature is unique. Laxman Sen himself was a poet and completed his father's unfinished works.

question: Why is Jagannath Temple of Puri called 'White Pagoda'?
options: Due to the white color of the temple, the main spire of the temple was whitewashed with lime, making it appear white from the sea.
White stone has been used there
solution: European sailors used Konark (Black Pagoda) and Puri (White Pagoda) for navigation while passing through the coast of Odisha.

question: In which direction does the Konark Sun Temple face so that the first rays of the sun fall on the sanctum sanctorum?
solution: The design of Konark temple is based on astronomy. On its main gate two huge lions are shown crushing elephants.

question: Which Sen ruler started 'Kulinism' in Bengal?
solution: Ballal Sen himself was a great scholar. He had composed the books named 'Danasagar' and 'Adbhutasagar'. Aristocracy influenced the social structure of Bengal for a long time.

question: Which style developed in the meeting place (Deccan) of 'Nagar style' and 'Dravidian style'?
solution: Vesara style temples are found mainly in the area between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers. The temples of Halebidu and Belur are the best examples of this.

question: 'Geet Govind' was composed by Jaidev, it is based on the love of which God?
solution: The meeting, separation and love of Radha and Krishna have been described in great detail in the twelve cantos of Geeta Govind. This is the greatest literary achievement of the Sen period.

question: What was the position of 'Vellalas' community in the society during the Chola period?
solution: The rich Vellalas were given titles like 'Muvendavelan' (one who served three kings) by the Chola kings.

question: 'Avantisundari', wife of 'Rajashekhar', was the princess of which dynasty and she herself was a great scholar?
solution: Avantisundari's scholarship can be gauged from the fact that Rajasekhar gave importance to her advice in his literary theories. This is evidence of the higher education of women in the contemporary society.

question: Who was the founder of the medieval Chola dynasty (850-1280 AD) who captured Thanjavur and built the Nishumbhasudani temple there?
solution: The initial capital of the Cholas was Uraiyur. They were under the Pallavas. Vijayalaya had assumed the title of 'Narakesari'. It is necessary to differentiate between the ancient Cholas and the medieval Cholas.

question: What was the capital of Lakshman Sen, the ruler of Sen dynasty after the fall of Pala dynasty?
solution: Laxman Sen is known for his generosity and love of literature. The invasion of Bakhtiyar Khilji during his reign marked the beginning of the medieval era in Bengal.

question: According to 'Agnikul Theory', at which place is the Gurjara-Pratihar dynasty believed to have originated?
solution: The founder of Gurjara-Pratihar dynasty was Nagabhata I. He successfully repelled Arab invasions from Sindh in the Battle of Rajasthan in the 8th century.

question: What were the wealthy merchants who headed the 'Nagaram' trading council during the Chola period called?
solution: Non-urban traders financed the Cholas' foreign campaigns and in return received commercial autonomy and protection.

question: Which ruler built the Sun Temple of Konark (Odisha) and what is it called?
options: Narasimha Deva I and the Black Pagoda
Bhimdev I and Modhera Sun Temple
solution: Konark temple is in the shape of a huge chariot which has 24 wheels. It is part of Kalinga architecture with features like rekha deul (spire) and pidha deul (pavilion).

question: At which place did Sen king Lakshman Sen establish the Vijay Stambh during his reign?
solution: Lakshman Sen conducted successful military campaigns up to Kashi (Varanasi) and Jagannath Puri, which mark the zenith of the military power of the Sen dynasty.

question: The present structure (white stone) of the Vishnupada temple located at 'Gaya' was built by Ahilyabai Holkar, but the inscription of which Pala ruler was originally found there?
solution: The Pala rulers, although Buddhist, also donated and patronized Hindu temples. This is a symbol of his secular rule.

question: By what name was the revenue officer of 'Nadu' (District) known in the Chola administration?
solution: The Chola revenue system was so precise that taxes were determined based on the quality of the soil of each farm. Land was confiscated if taxes were not paid.

question: Which tribe or community rebelled against 'Mahipal II' during the reign of Pala kings?
solution: The Kaivarta rebellion became one of the main reasons for the decline of the Pala dynasty. A leader named Divya killed Mahipala II and took control of North Bengal for some time.

question: What is the large pillared chamber in front of the main sanctum in 'Dravidian style' temples called?
solution: The pavilion was also used for dance (Bharatanatyam), music and as the court of the king. Chola temples were not only religious but also social and economic centres.

question: Who were called 'Taniyurs' within 'Nadu' during the Chola period?
options: The king's spies were called Ottar.
Large villages that were independent in administration
solution: Taniyar villages often developed around temples and were centers of economic and religious activity.

question: 'Mahodaya' was another name of which city during the Gurjara-Pratihar period?
solution: Palas, Pratiharas and Rashtrakutas fought for Kannauj only. The one who controlled Kannauj was considered the ruler of 'Sakal Uttarapath'.

question: Who was the one who came to India from Tibet and received education during the Pala Dynasty and later became an active monk of Nalanda?
solution: Cultural ties between India and Tibet were very strong during the Pala period. Tibetan kings had invited many Indian monks to their place.

question: The entrance of 'Dravidian style' temples is called 'Gopuram'. What was the shape of Gopuram during Chola period?
options: There were no sculptures in it
It was only at ground level
solution: The Gopurams of Meenakshi Temple of Madurai and Srirangam Temple are magnificent examples of Dravidian style. The gopuram contributed to both the beauty and security of the temple during the Chola period.

question: Which Pratihar king has been called 'Maharajadhiraja of Aryavarta' by 'Rajashekhar' in his plays?
solution: There was peace and prosperity during the time of Mahendrapala, which gave opportunity to art and literature to flourish. Rajasekhar has compared him with ancient emperors.

question: Who was called 'Perumkuri' in Chola administration?
options: The members of the Sabha were also called 'Perumakkal' who were the members of the supreme council of the village.
Tax collectors were known by different names.
This group of soldiers was called Padair.
The temple priests were called Adigal.
solution: The election of these members was done under very strict rules. It was essential for him to have deep knowledge of administration and law.
